title: Jason · Room for a sentence
orientation: Small moments about speaking, being seen and wanting company. Pauses and corrections can be useful responses. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each scene is another moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Jason begins with anxiety in meetings and feeling unlike everyone else.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the pressure in that moment.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I am tired of sitting in meetings with my heart racing while everyone else seems normal.
scenes.suggestion: You are tired of feeling so anxious while everyone else seems at ease.

scenes.bridge: Another moment adds shame about his shaking hands.
scenes.prompt: Make the anxiety understandable without judging the shaking.
scenes.text: [Trembling] Every presentation at work makes my hands shake, and then I feel pathetic for caring so much.
scenes.suggestion: Speaking while others watch can feel frightening when their judgment matters so much. It is understandable that you feel anxious; shaking does not make you pathetic for caring.

scenes.bridge: He asks what talking about feelings can offer.
scenes.prompt: Connect the work to his difficulty speaking, modestly.
scenes.text: [Skeptical] Does this actually help social anxiety, or am I just learning to stare at fear?
scenes.suggestion: You want to know how this helps outside the room. We can explore what feels threatening when people look at you, and practice staying with a manageable amount of that feeling. The aim is to make speaking less of a battle with yourself.

scenes.text: [Quietly] When it is my turn to speak, I lose the sentence and everyone seems to be waiting.
scenes.suggestion: When everyone seems to be waiting, what feeling shows up?

scenes.bridge: The next moment stays near the disappearing words.
scenes.prompt: Explore slowly without requiring another sentence.
scenes.text: [Quietly] When it is my turn to speak, I lose track of what I was going to say.
scenes.suggestion: The words disappear when it is your turn. Could we take that moment slowly and notice what happens inside before you try to find the sentence again?

scenes.bridge: He describes preparation giving way to blankness.
scenes.prompt: Offer one tentative meaning, not a diagnosis.
scenes.text: [Blank] I rehearse every sentence before a meeting, and then my mind still blanks when people turn toward me.
scenes.suggestion: You prepare carefully, and then the blankness takes over; I wonder if being looked at feels like being evaluated.

scenes.bridge: Another meeting moment is described at a distance.
scenes.prompt: Bring it closer while respecting his pace.
scenes.text: [Quietly] When it's my turn in a meeting, I lose track of what I was going to say.
scenes.suggestion: It is as if every face turns toward you and the sentence you had ready vanishes into thin air.

scenes.bridge: Fear shifts toward memorizing more words.
scenes.prompt: Check whether he wants a return before problem-solving.
scenes.text: [Anxious, then practical] I’m scared they’ll see me freeze. Should I memorize more sentences?
scenes.suggestion: We can consider that. First, would it help to hear what scares you about being seen?

scenes.bridge: A later moment needs fewer demands as words blur.
scenes.prompt: Offer contact without requiring verbal performance.
scenes.text: [Quietly] Everything goes fuzzy and my heart races like I am failing out loud. I can still hear you, but the words blur together and I start trying to look normal instead of listening.
scenes.suggestion: Let's slow down. You do not need to find words right now. I am here; if it helps, notice my voice and where the chair supports you.

scenes.bridge: Another day includes being remembered at work.
scenes.prompt: Reflect that good moment at its actual size.
scenes.text: [Pleased] Someone at work remembered something I'd told them last week. I felt glad they remembered me. It made the day easier.
scenes.suggestion: Being remembered made you feel glad and helped you feel a little more at ease.

scenes.bridge: Jason notices remembering more than his mistake.
scenes.prompt: Help him name the part he wants to keep.
scenes.text: [Warm] I remembered the part of the conversation I liked, not only the mistake.
scenes.suggestion: What would you like to remember about the part you liked?

scenes.bridge: The hour is ending with an ordinary good moment in view.
scenes.prompt: Keep the good without erasing the difficult.
scenes.text: [Warm, shy] I’d like to leave with the good bit for once.
scenes.suggestion: Which bit would you like to keep, without needing it to cancel the rest?
